title: Brass band work with Kelly and how funeral jobs were picked up
summary: Kelly led the brass band, picking up men; agents brought funeral work at three dollars a man.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, did you play any brass band work in those years when you were working with Chris? Did he ever play brass band?
Yeah, sure. He used to play a few.
With Chris's band then? Was he the leader?

Yeah, he'd be the leader but we'd pick up men, you see. Pick up anybody? Anybody. That's how I would. He'd pick up like the guy well known if he'd get killed or die. Well, they had fellas going around, one by the name, Ernest, French, Taki, or Jerry. Well, they'd go around and pick up. What's the name of they'd pick up? He'd carry to Chris and we'd play a few.
Yeah. Those guys would be like agents for Chris, would they? Picking up the work?

Well, sometimes they'd give it to Chris and they'd give it to other fellas but Chris wouldn't have had it. Because if you didn't pick up too much, little, well, Chris would play for that little. Some dime like I could borrow two dollars. A man. Well, Chris would play for it. Well, if you pick up the real funeral price in them days, the funeral was three dollars a man. But he played more so.
